# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
2. **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
3. **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
4. **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
5. **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)
- **CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV** – Main Street: clicking a tutorial button should not pass through to the cards below (completed)
- Repo file matches: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0-hud-2dp/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN-peek/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (contextual).

## Goal (user story)

When a player boots Main Street, the Day Start banner ('Day 1') and its click SFX fire immediately — before the player has had a chance to choose how to begin (run the tutorial, skip, resume a checkpoint, or start fresh). The banner should only play once the game actually starts.

## Root cause

`create()` (and the async campaign-load path in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) call `s.startDayPhase()` at boot, each firing `MainStreetAnimator.animateDayBanner` (visual + CLICK SFX) before the tutorial-offer modal / resume overlay is shown. Up to two banners play before any player choice.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Booting the scene fires NO Day-N banner (visual or SFX) before the player has chosen how to start: boot-time `startDayPhase` calls are banner-suppressed.
2. The banner plays once the game actually starts: (a) Start Tutorial, (b) Skip for Now (free play), (c) fresh start with no eligible offer modal.
3. Checkpoint Resume shows no banner (same day continues — already suppressed via skipMarketRefill) and discards any boot deferral.
4. Day-transition banners on subsequent days (End Turn → next day start) still play, including difficulty-change restarts.
5. Reduced-motion and replay/headless behavior unchanged (animator handles both internally).
6. Full test suite green: unit 283 files / 5244 tests; browser suites (day-banner 5/5 incl. 2 new regression tests); tutorial E2E parts 1-6.

## Implementation summary (authored directly, uncommitted — pending formal implement-skill worktree/commit)

- `MainStreetTurnController.startDayPhase(skipMarketRefill, suppressDayBanner)` — new param gates the banner.
- Boot-time call sites (create tail + both loadCampaignAndSetup branches) pass `suppressDayBanner=true`.
- `MainStreetScene.deferredDayBanner` + `playDeferredDayBanner()` — presents the deferred banner when the player starts (tutorial skip) or starts fresh with no modal; cleared (not played) on tutorial start / checkpoint resume.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManager.showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner()` — replaces raw showIfEligible call sites (5) so the deferred banner plays whenever no offer modal appears.
- 2 new browser regression tests in `tests/main-street/day-banner.browser.test.ts` (banner silent while modal waits; banner plays once skipped).

## Environment issue found (blocked full-suite runs)

Removed stale, completed worktree `wl-CG-0MSW6HZ6G006PK6I-test-contract` whose `.worklog` symlink looped to the root `.worklog`, causing ELOOP crashes in vitest browser runs. Reverted worktree is gone; branch metadata left intact. Belongs to completed item 'Test contract: single-row market & hand flows' (CG-0MSW6HZ6G006PK6I) — operator may want to record there.
data.title: Day One banner and sound effects play before game actually starts

# Speed up browser tests and create test profiles

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Task**

> Browser tests take ~15 min (92 files). Profile: smoke (30s), dev (3 min), ci (full). Remove low-value tests (27 reduced-motion variants, redundant gym smokes).

## Current State

- 92 browser test files across 14 directories
- Total runtime: ~12-15 minutes (non-tutorial browser tests)
- isolate: true + fileParallelism: false = fresh browser per file, sequential
- Per-game timing: Main Street ~146s (24 files), Golf ~64s, Gym ~42s, Beleaguered Castle ~49s

## Problems

1. Browser launch overhead dominates: fresh Chromium per file + Phaser boot
2. Sequential execution blocks fast tests on slow ones
3. 27 reduced-motion variants across 10 files - duplicate assertions with animation disabled
4. Gym tests (19 files) check rendering/boots, not game play
5. No test profiles - developers wait 15 min for feedback

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Three Test Profiles

- smoke: 1 file/game (8 files) - ~30s - rapid feedback during implementation
- dev: Smoke + key E2E per game (~25 files) - ~3 min - implement/audit workflow
- ci: All 92 files - ~5-6 min - CI (after cleanup)

### 2. Remove Low-Value Tests (27 tests, 10 files)

Reduced-motion variants that duplicate main test assertions:
- incident-reveal.browser.test.ts - 7 reduced-motion variants
- click-place.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- market-deal-in.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- sell-demolition.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- event-played.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- synergy-formation.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- upgrade-level-up.browser.test.ts - 2 reduced-motion variants
- day-banner.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- income-collection.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants

### 3. Optimizations

a) Merge reduced-motion variants into parent tests
b) Share game instances within test files (reduce game boots via beforeEach)
c) Reduce gym from 19 files to 1 smoke + 1 feature file
d) Tutorial E2E tests (7 files) excluded from smoke/dev profiles

### 4. Implementation Steps

1. Create run-smoke-tests.sh / run-dev-tests.sh with vitest project filters
2. Remove reduced-motion variant tests (27 tests)
3. Merge remaining tests to share game instances
4. Reduce gym tests
5. Update package.json scripts
6. Update docs/DEVELOPER.md

## Key Files

- vite.config.ts: vitest browser test configuration (isolate, fileParallelism, timeout)
- package.json: test scripts (add test:smoke, test:dev)
- scripts/run-ci-tests.sh: CI test runner (add smoke/dev stages)
- tests/**/*.browser.test.ts: browser test files to review for removal

# Community Favour — Engine Action, State, and Config

## Goal
Implement the core `community-favour` player action type: exchange coins ↔ reputation with per-difficulty configurable rates, MarketPhase gating, and a once-per-turn guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — PlayerAction union:** A new `CommunityFavourAction` variant is added to the `PlayerAction` union in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
  ```
  | { type: 'community-favour'; direction: 'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins' }
  ```

- **AC2 — executeAction case:** A `case 'community-favour'` is added to `executeAction()` that:
  - Validates the state is in `MarketPhase` (throws if not).
  - Checks `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false` (throws if true).
  - Validates resource sufficiency via the `EconomyLedger`:
    - `coins-to-rep`: checks `coins >= favourCoinsToRepCost`.
    - `rep-to-coins`: checks `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost`.
  - Applies the exchange:
    - `coins-to-rep`: subtracts `favourCoinsToRepCost` coins, adds `1` reputation.
    - `rep-to-coins`: subtracts `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` reputation, adds `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain` coins.
  - Sets `state.favourUsedThisTurn = true`.
  - Does **not** decrement `actionsRemaining` (free once-per-turn action).

- **AC3 — State field:** `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` is added to `MainStreetState` and the serialized state `MainStreetSerializedState`.

- **AC4 — DayStart reset:** In `executeDayStart()`, `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is reset to `false` (alongside `actionsRemaining` reset).

- **AC5 — GameConfig constants:** Per-difficulty exchange rates are added to `GameConfig` and all presets in `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`:
  - `favourCoinsToRepCost: number` — coins consumed for 1 rep (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsRepCost: number` — reputation consumed for coin gain (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain: number` — coins gained when spending rep (default: 3).
  - All 4 presets (easy, normal, medium, hard) include these values.

- **AC6 — MarketPhase gating:** The action is only legal during `MarketPhase`; the `case` throws an appropriate error for other phases.

- **AC7 — Once-per-turn enforcement:** The `favourUsedThisTurn` flag prevents a second exchange until the next `DayStart`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — PlayerAction union, case handler, executeAction logic
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — favourUsedThisTurn field, serialization, DayStart reset
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — GameConfig constants and all presets
data.title: Engine: Community Favour action, state, and config

# Hint text obscured by hand

## Problem Statement

When placing a card from hand (in `placing-from-hand` or `placing-business` UI phases), the inline hint text rendered at `actionY - 4` is visually obscured by the hand card sprites themselves, making it unreadable.

## User Story

As a player, I need to clearly see the instruction text telling me where to place the card I'm holding, so I can complete the action without confusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase-specific hint text ("Card in hand (N) — click an empty slot to place" and "Place \"[card name]\" -- click an empty slot") is no longer rendered inline at the action area.
2. The hint text is displayed using the shared `HintBar` component at the bottom of the screen instead.
3. When the UI phase changes from `placing-from-hand` or `placing-business` back to `market`, the hint bar text is reset to the standard instruction.
4. All existing tests pass.

## Constraints

- Must use the existing `HintBar` component (`src/ui/HintBar.ts`) — no new positioning or custom text rendering.
- Minimal change: only modify `MainStreetRenderer.ts`.
- No behavior change beyond repositioning the text.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/HintBar.ts` — shared hint bar component, positioned at bottom-centre by default.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` lines 1534, 1559 — inline hint text rendered via `s.add.text(rightX, by - 4, ...)` into `s.actionContainer`, positioned near the hand.
- `s.hintBar` — already instantiated at line 292 of `MainStreetRenderer.ts`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Remove inline hint text creation in `placing-from-hand` and `placing-business` branches; call `s.hintBar.setText()` instead.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHint.ts` — May need updates if hint text is referenced elsewhere for these phases.

## Related Work

None found — this is an isolated UI fix.

# Activity log no longer scrolls

## Problem statement

The Main Street activity log no longer auto-scrolls to show the latest content. New log entries (income, incident results, purchases, staff costs, etc.) accumulate off-screen at the bottom of the panel while the view stays pinned at the top showing the earliest entries, so the player cannot see the most recent game events without manually wheel-scrolling.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — rely on the activity log to see the latest game events (turn headers, income, incident results, purchase/pay effects, win/loss).
- **Tutorial/review users** — use the log to verify that their actions took effect.

### User stories

- "As a player, when I buy a card or an incident resolves, I want the log to scroll so I can see the new entry without manual scrolling."
- "As a player, when I scroll up to re-read an older entry, I don't want the log to yank me back down on the next event."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When new log entries are added while the player is at (or near) the bottom of the log, the log auto-scrolls so the newest entry is visible.
2. When the player has scrolled up to read history, adding a new entry must NOT steal their scroll position (auto-scroll stays paused until they return to the bottom).
3. When the player wheel-scrolls back to the bottom, auto-scroll re-engages for subsequent entries.
4. On scene restart / new game, the log renders correctly with no content scrolled off the top of the panel (no regression of CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z).
5. Behavior is covered by automated tests (unit/browser): the existing browser tests that codify the current non-auto-scrolling behaviour are updated to assert the restored auto-scroll behaviour.
6. Full project test suite (`npm test`) and production build (`npm run build`) pass with the changes.
7. Relevant documentation (code comments in `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`, and any activity-log guidance in `docs/`) is updated to reflect the restored behaviour.

## Constraints

- Preserve the "don't yank the reader" UX: auto-scroll must engage only when the user is at/near the bottom (existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism — do not replace it).
- Preserve the scene-restart safety fix from CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z (stale scroll state must not hide all entries on restart).
- Main Street only; no engine/other-game impact expected.

## Existing state

- `logAutoScroll` starts `false` (MainStreetScene.ts line 117, reset in MainStreetLifecycleManager.create ~line 185).
- `refreshLog()` (MainStreetRenderer.ts ~line 1627): on overflow, keeps `logScrollOffset` clamped at its current value when `logAutoScroll` is false, then sets `logAutoScroll = (logScrollOffset >= logMaxScroll - 4)`. Because the offset starts at 0 (top) and content overflows by more than 4px, `atBottom` is false → `logAutoScroll` stays false forever; the log never moves until the user wheel-scrolls to the bottom (which re-engages it via `handleLogWheel`).
- Browser tests codify this behaviour: `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` ("does not position content above the log display area when entries first overflow" asserts `logAutoScroll === false` and offset stays 0; "auto-scroll snaps to bottom..." manually sets `logAutoScroll = true`, masking the real flow).

## Root cause (regression)

Commit `0b642a6e` — CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z ("Fix initial logAutoScroll to false to prevent content scrolling off the top") changed the initial `logAutoScroll` from `true` to `false` in both `MainStreetScene.ts` and `MainStreetLifecycleManager.create()`. Its stated assumption — "auto-scroll kicks in naturally when the user scrolls to the bottom" — is wrong for the default flow: the `atBottom` re-enable check in `refreshLog` never becomes true while the offset stays pinned at the top, so auto-scroll never engages. History: `git log -S "logAutoScroll = true"` → the original was `true` (0bd7eaf6), so this is a behavioural regression.

## Desired change

Restore "start at the bottom (latest entries) and auto-scroll on new entries unless the user has scrolled up":

- Set the initial `logAutoScroll` back to `true` (class property + create() reset), **and** ensure the scene-restart case still clamps correctly (the existing `Phaser.Math.Clamp` branch already guards stale offsets; worst case a restart resets offsets to 0 with an empty/new log so maxScroll recomputes to 0 — safe).
- Keep `handleLogWheel`'s re-engage-on-bottom logic unchanged.
- Update the browser tests that assert the current non-scrolling behaviour, and add a regression test that reproduces the real flow (fresh scene → entries accumulate → offset reaches bottom / latest visible without manual scroll), plus a test for "scrolled up → new entry does not yank position".
- Sanity-check the mask/visibility safety net still renders correctly at the bottom.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logAutoScroll` property initial value (line 117).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — scene-create reset of `logAutoScroll` (~line 185).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshLog()` scroll bounds/auto-scroll logic (~lines 1627–1720).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — `handleLogWheel` bottom re-engage threshold (reference, likely unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — update tests codifying current behaviour; add regression tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — restart test asserts container `y > 0`; verify still valid after the change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z** — "Activity log extends beyond the bottom of the content area" (completed) — the commit (`0b642a6e`) that introduced this regression; its acceptance criteria include the restart-safety requirement that must not regress.
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** — "Undo/redo feedback notification" (completed) — logged as related by `/skill:find-related`; UI feedback adjacent, no functional dependency.
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** / **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** — surfaced by `/skill:find-related` (score-threshold noise; not functionally related to log scrolling).
- Original scroll implementation precedent (git ref, not a worklog item): commit `0bd7eaf6` (CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 "Add activity log with state tracking, engine instrumentation, UI panel, and tests") — initial `logAutoScroll = true`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "scrolls to show the latest content" means the log default view is the bottom (newest entries), with auto-scroll on new entries while the user is at the bottom — i.e. restoring the pre-0b642a6e UX. This matches the bug title ("no longer scrolls") and standard log-panel convention.
- **Assumption:** current priority `medium` is appropriate (non-blocking, user-facing UX regression); may be re-considered to `high` if gameplay clarity is deemed significant by the producer.
- **Risk (scope creep):** restoring `logAutoScroll = true` may re-expose the original "content off the top" restart symptom if clamping is insufficient — mitigate with the existing clamp + explicit restart coverage, not by rebuilding the scroll system.
- **Risk:** other tests may implicitly depend on the log starting at the top (e.g. `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` restart test asserting `logContentContainer.y > 0`); verify and adjust assertions rather than behaviour.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the log default to showing the latest entries (bottom) — i.e. restore the pre-regression behaviour — as implied by the report?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes (documented above).** The bug title ("used to scroll to show the latest content … no longer automatically does so") states the expected behaviour directly, and the pre-regression implementation (`logAutoScroll = true`) matches it. Source: work item CG-0MT24HFNM002MPF5 description + git archaeology (commit `0b642a6e` vs `0bd7eaf6`).
- Q: "Should auto-scroll pause while the user reads older entries (standard UX)?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes.** The existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism and `handleLogWheel` already implement this; the fix merely restores its initial state. Source: code inspection of `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`.
---
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** – Undo/redo feedback notification (completed)
- **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** – [test-failure] Replay CLI tests in tests/replay/replay.test.ts (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts exceeds 15s) — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** – Remove time-limited play mechanics (maxTurns) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: automatically, content, latest, log, longer, scroll, show, used
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: automatically, content, latest, log, scroll, show, used
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: activity, content, log, longer, scroll, show, used

# Monte Carlo sanity-check and full-suite verification

Parent: CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA (Main Street: reputation score multiplier (x5) should become a simple count)

## Goal

Verify the reputation multiplier removal end-to-end: re-run the Monte Carlo harness to sanity-check balance impact (score deflation expected — do NOT gate on exact parity), verify income-side multipliers are behaviourally unchanged (scope guard), and confirm the full test suite and build are green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run monte-carlo` runs clean; win-rate/score distributions recorded in a work-item comment with score deflation documented as expected (no parity gating).
- [ ] Games still reach a decisive endpoint under the retuned 100/120/150 thresholds (win/lose outcomes present, no pathological non-termination flagged by the harness).
- [ ] Income-side reputation multipliers verified unchanged: targeted tests for `applyReputationMultiplier` (1 + rep/20, capped x3) and `rep-multiplier` income effect produce identical results to pre-change expectations.
- [ ] Full `npm test` (unit + browser + tutorial E2E) passes and `npm run build` succeeds at the final commit.

## Key Files

- example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts
- tests/main-street/ (all, via full suite)
- docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json (reference, may be regenerated by harness run)

## Notes

- This is a verification slice, not a code-change slice; it blocks on F2 and F3.
- No gate on score parity — the operator explicitly accepted score deflation.

## Problem statement

`npm run monte-carlo` (and `monte-carlo-sweep`) fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because `tsx` does not understand Vite's `?raw` query suffix used to import `card-data.csv` in `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Users

- **TCE developer** running Monte Carlo balance analysis: expects `npm run monte-carlo` to produce `results/main-street-monte-carlo.json` and `.csv`.
- **CI/automated tooling** (future): may run the harness headlessly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo -- --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --strategy greedy --out results/main-street-monte-carlo.json --csv-out results/main-street-monte-carlo.csv` completes successfully (exit 0) and produces valid output files.
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep -- --sweep --seeds 100 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --out results/sweep.json --csv-out results/sweep.csv` completes successfully (exit 0).
3. `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript + Vite production build).
4. Full test suite `npm test` passes.

## Constraints

- The fix should use `vite-node` (already proven to work; documented in `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67).
- Per the Doc-Update Policy, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` scripts list must be updated if scripts change.
- Do not modify `tsx` or add loader hooks — that is more fragile and less established.

## Existing state

- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` imports Main Street game code which uses `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw';`
- `package.json` defines `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` scripts using `tsx`.
- `vite-node` works for the same import (used by `scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`).

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` npm scripts in `package.json` from `tsx` to `vite-node`. Update documentation (DEVELOPER.md, AGENTS.md) to reflect the change.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Change `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` script commands.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update script listings to reflect `vite-node` usage.
- `AGENTS.md` — Update scripts list to reflect `vite-node` usage.

## Related work

- Discovered from: CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW (Monte Carlo sanity check)
- Sibling pattern: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 documents `vite-node` usage for a similar import path.
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1-F4 work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Why not fix tsx instead of switching to vite-node?" — Answer: tsx does not support Vite `?raw` queries natively; adding a loader hook is fragile and unmaintainable. vite-node is the established pattern in this repo (see `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`). Source: code review of `MainStreetCards.ts` and `card-catalog.md`.
- Q: "Are there other `tsx` scripts that might also break on `?raw` imports?" — Answer: No — `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `scripts/replay.ts` and `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` are the only scripts using `tsx`. The `export-transcripts.ts` does not import Main Street code. `replay.ts` may import Main Street but does not import `?raw` CSV. Source: grep of `scripts/` for `tsx` and `?raw`.

# Intake Brief: Main Street: npm run monte-carlo (tsx) fails on ?raw CSV imports

## Headline

`npm run monte-carlo` fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because tsx cannot load the Vite-style `card-data.csv?raw` import; switch the affected npm scripts from tsx to vite-node (the verified, in-repo-precedented runner) and update docs per the Doc-Update Policy.

## Problem statement

Three npm scripts that transitively import `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, `save-load-smoke`) fail under tsx with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. tsx's loader misparses the Vite `?raw` query suffix for non-TS/TXT extensions, treating the CSV as a JS module. Root cause is in the import chain (`MainStreetCards.ts` line 18: `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`), not in the harness logic — the same harness runs correctly under vite-node.

## Users

- **Developer running balance validation** — "I want `npm run monte-carlo` to just work so I can verify card balance after rebalancing card-data.csv." Example story: after editing `card-data.csv`, a developer runs `npm run monte-carlo` (or `monte-carlo-sweep`) and gets the JSON + CSV outputs described in docs.
- **Developer running the save/load smoke check** — "I want `npm run save-load-smoke` to pass so I can quickly verify persistence round-trips." Currently it crashes with the same loader error before running any scenario.
- **Producer/CI reader** — wants the documented commands in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` to remain accurate and working.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo` completes successfully end-to-end with the default settings (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, greedy, maxTurns 25) and writes both JSON and CSV outputs; results are consistent with the verified working control run (200/200 runs; winRate 38.5%, medianScore 55.8, avgNoActionTurns 0 — i.e., determinism preserved, no balance drift).
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep` completes successfully in sweep mode (strategy × difficulty combinations) and writes its outputs.
3. `npm run save-load-smoke` completes successfully (exit 0, failures 0) — same root cause, same fix; expanded blast radius captured in this item.
4. Spot-check that unaffected tsx workflows still work (`npm run replay` or `balance-cards`) — no collateral regression from the runner switch.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, AGENTS.md scripts list, and docs/DEVELOPER.md, per the Doc-Update Policy; the vite-node rationale is documented in the same style as `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- The npm script **names and CLI flags must not change** (`npm run monte-carlo`, `--seeds/--seed-prefix/--maxTurns/--strategy/--out/--csv-out`, `--sweep`, etc.) — the harness CLI is a documented interface.
- Testing/validation criterion preserved: seeded determinism must be maintained (same seed → same deal order → same outputs; no reliance on RNG ordering changes).
- Prefer the established runner pattern over bespoke tooling: **vite-node** is the in-repo precedent for scripts that import `MainStreetCards.ts` (see `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` already uses it for exactly this reason) and is verified working for both broken entry points. A custom tsx loader hook for `?raw` would work but is more complex, repo-specific, and has no precedent — evaluated and rejected as the primary path.
- Doc-Update Policy applies (package.json scripts change).

## Existing state

- `package.json` lines 17–18, 21: `monte-carlo` / `monte-carlo-sweep` = `tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts ...`; `save-load-smoke` = `tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` line 18 imports `./card-data.csv?raw` (Vite bundler syntax, docs comment: "bundled at build time via Vite's `?raw`").
- Import chains that break under tsx: `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` → `MainStreetMonteCarlo` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`; `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`.
- Reproduced failures: `npx tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `npx tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` both exit 1 with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` (Node v22.22.1).
- Verified working: `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/monte-carlo.ts --seeds 200 ...` (200/200; winRate 38.5%) and `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` (failures 0).
- Tests are unaffected — vitest handles `?raw` via Vite (e.g. `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`).
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b (before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1–F4) and at HEAD.

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, and `save-load-smoke` package.json scripts from `tsx` to `vite-node` (entry scripts stay unchanged). Update docs per the Doc-Update Policy (AGENTS.md scripts list, docs/DEVELOPER.md; add the vite-node rationale for MainStreetCards-importing scripts in the same style as card-catalog.md). No engine or game code changes expected.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — scripts lines 17–18 (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`) and 21 (`save-load-smoke`): tsx → vite-node.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — root cause location (`import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`); likely unchanged, but should be re-verified and its "bundled at build time" comment cross-referenced.
- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` — entry points; unchanged, but verification targets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (lines ~197, ~230), `AGENTS.md` (scripts list, line ~76) — doc updates per Doc-Update Policy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) — precedent/template for documenting the vite-node rationale.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY — DUPLICATE** (status open): identical description, created 7 seconds earlier — a double-submit of this item. Producer to resolve (likely close in favour of this item, CG-0MT4RBHQR006C5GR).
- CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW — "Monte Carlo sanity-check and full-suite verification" (open, in_progress): the discovering item; this bug was found while verifying it. `discovered-from` relationship already recorded.
- CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA — "Main Street: reputation score multiplier" (in_progress, plan_complete): commit b2bec26b predates this work; bug reproduced before and after it (pre-existing, not a regression of that item).
- CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY — "Replay CLI tests ... (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm ...)" (completed): related tsx CLI tooling context.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — documents the vite-node precedent for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (approach):** vite-node is the chosen fix over a tsx `?raw` loader hook — based on in-repo precedent (card-catalog.md), verified success on both broken scripts, and lower maintenance surface. If the producer prefers the loader-hook approach, scope is limited to the monte-carlo/save-load-smoke invocations and the doc updates shrink accordingly.
- **Assumption (scope):** fixing `save-load-smoke` in the same item is in-scope — same root cause, same fix, verified working under vite-node. If the producer wants to split it, create a child item.
- **Risk:** switching runners could subtly change module resolution for other `@alias` imports in the chain — mitigated by the verification ACs (output parity with the control run; full test suite) and by the existing precedent (vite-node already used for a MainStreetCards-importing generator).
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to harness logic, balance logic, or CSV handling are in scope; any balance-tuning opportunities surfaced by the working harness are separate work items (see CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview-driven questions were not required — the seed context (goal, confirmed working path, likely fix options) plus repo verification sufficed to draft the brief. Decisions recorded for auditability:

- Q: "Fix via vite-node or a custom tsx loader hook?" — Answer (research, no user input needed): **vite-node**. Evidence: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 explicitly documents vite-node for `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` "(uses Vite-aware ESM loader because it imports deck-building functions from MainStreetCards.ts)" — the identical situation; both broken entry points verified green under vite-node. Loader-hook alternative has no precedent and higher maintenance; recorded as evaluated-and-rejected.
- Q: "Does the bug affect scripts beyond monte-carlo?" — Answer (repo verification): **yes — `npm run save-load-smoke` fails with the identical error** (transitively imports `MainStreetCards` via `MainStreetState`); verified green under vite-node. Included in ACs as in-scope via same-fix. `replay`, `export-transcripts`, `run-balance-cards` verified unaffected (no `?raw` chain).
- Q: "Duplicate work item CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY?" — Answer (evidence): identical description, created 7 s before this item, same discovered-from — a double-submit. Flagged to the producer for resolution; not blocking this intake.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSP1HCAS00785MP** – Synergy bonuses should count diagonally adjacent slots on the Main Street street grid (completed)
- **CG-0MSQJ7QLM0076FTD** – Group D: Incident events — polarity-balanced (10 cards) (completed)

# Banking mechanics — unit test suite

Test-first feature for **Main Street: action banking (bank unused actions for future turns)** (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR). New `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts` covering every banking acceptance criterion; update existing AI/MC budget tests so they remain meaningful and correct under passive banking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 · Banking on end-of-turn (test):** every unspent action in the day's budget banks — tests cover 0 / some / nearly-all actions taken (3 available, 1 taken → 2 banked); a fully-spent day banks 0.
- **AC2 · Cap enforced (test):** `bankedActions` never exceeds 2 in tests — further accumulation is discarded (end a day at cap with leftovers → stays 2); the bank cannot grow past the cap.
- **AC3 · Day-start composition (test):** tests assert day budget = 1 base + staff `actionsPerTurn` bonus + `bankedActions` capped 2 (banked 2 + GM → 4; banked 2 without GM → 3).
- **AC4 · Staff actions used first (test):** with General Manager employed (+1 `actionsPerTurn`), idle/partial days bank only the base 1 — the staff bonus never banks (idle GM day banks 1, not 2; GM day with 1 spent banks 1).
- **AC6 · State + persistence (test):** `bankedActions` round-trips save/load (legacy saves default to 0); undo/redo command snapshot/restore restores bank + `actionsRemaining` without double-banking.
- **AC7 · Quality gates (existing tests stay green):** updated `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` assertions are banking-aware (passive AI banks leftover actions, so later-day budgets exceed the old `maxPerDay <= 1` no-GM bound); `action-economy.test.ts` (full-budget-spend scenarios), `ai-strategy`, integration and Monte Carlo tests verified green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Mirror the patterns in `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts`: `setupMainStreetGame`, `executeDayStart(state, skipMarketRefill)`, `executeAction`, `processEndOfTurn`, `serializeMainStreetState`/`deserializeMainStreetState`, `gmTemplate()`.
- Use seeded setup for determinism; exercise banking across multi-day sequences (DayStart → spend → processEndOfTurn → DayStart again).
- Update `ai-action-budget.test.ts` budget assertions to assert banking-aware daily budgets (legit carry-over per the passive-AI rule; not arbitrary baselines).

## Dependencies

- None (TDD — written against intended behavior; may be authored alongside features 2–3 in the same worktree).

## Deliverables

- New test file + updated existing budget tests; all unit tests green.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play a competitive mode against an AI opponent who builds businesses on the **same street**, so that turns give me more to do and the game has a rival to race against.

## Design scope (from feasibility analysis, 2025-07 session)

- **Shared street grid** (10 slots); each placed business is owned by one player; income from a business accrues to its **owner**.
- **Events affect the whole street**: investment events and incidents keep the existing street-wide resolution semantics, but income/damage must be routed per-owner.
- **Staff are player-only**: the AI does not hire staff, and its competitive decision space excludes staff actions (hire-staff, peek).
- **Single shared market row**: buying a card denies it to the opponent (market competition is a first-class feature).
- **Alternating turn structure** — design decision to confirm at intake: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day vs. alternating full days.

## Reusability findings (basis for this item)

- The decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `enumerateLegalActions`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) transfers ~1:1 — it is UI-free and already shared between the Monte Carlo harness and the hint system.
- The state/engine layers are single-owner: `MainStreetState` has one resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining; `applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions` all assume one owner. These need a per-player split plus owner-tagged grid slots.
- Greedy heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street (`scoreBusinessAction = (income+synergy)*horizon - cost`; `aiPlanningHorizon` reads a single score) — scoring must become ownership-aware.
- PRD M3 (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`) explicitly scoped "AI vs. player (competitive mode)" as N/A — this item is a deliberate scope extension; note it in the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- AC1: A competitive-mode state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG.
- AC2: The AI opponent plays a legal full turn through the existing strategy layer (`enumerateLegalActions` → scored choice → `executeAction`), with staff actions excluded.
- AC3: Income accrues to the owner of each business; street-wide events/incidents affect both players under the shared-street semantics.
- AC4: A head-to-head Monte Carlo harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) measures the win distribution across >=200 seeds to validate competitive balance.
- AC5 (scene, may be split into a child at planning): competitive mode is selectable from the game selector, renders the shared street with owner colouring, alternates turns, and animates AI turns with SFX per the audio/feedback rule (AGENTS.md best practice 8).
data.title: Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30).

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold.
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Deterministic validation: extend `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (or a sibling harness) to run head-to-head AI-vs-AI and, where feasible, AI-vs-baseline matches across >=200 seeds; document win/score distributions.

## Out of scope (decision to record in item)

Whether to add opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — record an explicit in/out decision with rationale; denial can be a follow-up child if in.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- AC2: Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the shared single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- AC3: A deterministic head-to-head Monte Carlo harness runs the adapted strategy against a baseline over >=200 seeds and produces win/score distribution metrics (extension of `MainStreetMonteCarloMetrics` or equivalent).
- AC4: All existing single-player AI tests (ai-strategy, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.
data.title: Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play

# Unit Tests: Composite Pricing Parity

Comprehensive unit tests covering the pricing parity changes for same-turn buy-and-play.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Test: composite charges premium for business cards** — A same-day, just-moved business card placed from hand to street via the click composite deducts the +50% premium (Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2), not listed cost. Verifies the coin balance, action count, and log message.
- [ ] **Test: composite charges premium for community-space cards** — Same-day just-moved community-space card placed from hand to street via the click composite deducts the +50% premium. (Previously, drag-drop was the only route applying premium to community-space.)
- [ ] **Test: premium rejected when unaffordable** — When the player cannot afford the premium price, the composite placement is rejected with illegal-move feedback (insufficient coins), coin balance unchanged, and the dialog does not fire (pre-gate check).
- [ ] **Test: held-card play stays listed cost** — A business card held in hand from a previous day (not same-day) placed via the click composite deducts listed cost and consumes 1 action. pendingHandJustMoved is false for held cards.
- [ ] **Test: GM two-action listed-cost path** — When the player is a GM with 2 actions available and uses one to move the card to hand, the second action at placement deducts listed cost (no premium). The composite and GM path are priced identically.
- [ ] **Test: parity with drag-drop** — The composite price for a same-day card equals buyAndPlaceBusiness drag-drop price for the same card. Invariant: drag is never cheaper than click.
- [ ] **Test: dialog preference persists** — The "Don't show this again" dismissal is persisted (localStorage or SettingsStore-style) and the dialog does not fire on subsequent premium-incurring buy-and-play.
- [ ] **All unit tests pass** — Full test suite completes.

## Key Files

- tests/main-street/composite-pricing.test.ts — new test file (or append to existing MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts / action-economy.test.ts)
- src/ui/SettingsStore.ts or example-games/main-street/MainStreetPrefs.ts — preference persistence pattern

## Dependencies

- Depends on the engine changes landing (children for engine and turn controller) — tests are written first but implementation must exist to verify.

Discovered during audit of CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (discovered-from:CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK).

The audit skill's child persistence path (persist_audit.py -> wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no) unconditionally triggers wl's revertToPlanComplete() (WL-0MSKHYI5U0069FVV): any completed/in_review item with an audit verdict 'No' is reverted to open/plan_complete, and its dependency-descendants are auto-blocked.

Impact observed: an infra-fallback run (audit semaphore concurrency limit) persisted 'No' for all 9 children of CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK at 16:37:41-50Z, demoting all 9 from completed/in_review to open/blocked + plan_complete. An infra-fallback 'No' is not an explicit model assessment (SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V) and must not demote. Children were manually restored 2026-08-24.

ACs:
1. Audit runner/persist path for child audits distinguishes infra-fallback 'No' from genuine model 'No' and does not demote children on the former (restore semantics per SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V applied to children).
2. When a parent audit persists child verdicts, child lifecycle transitions are only applied when the verdict is a genuine model assessment; descendants are not auto-blocked by stale/fallback child audits.
3. A regression test covers: child at completed/in_review + parent-persisted fallback 'No' child audit -> child stays completed/in_review and descendants stay unblocked.
4. Documented in AGENTS.md / audit skill SKILL.md that wl audit-set carries its own revert side-effect; persist path must neutralize it (e.g. pass explicit stage/if-stage guard or restore after).
data.title: Audit infra: wl audit-set 'no' reverts parent-persisted child audits, demoting completed/in_review children (and descendants blocked)
